text:
Thessaly Weir diverts the Morrow River, according to a project update circulated Thursday by Helio Basin Authority. The upgrade lifts seasonal diversion capacity to 18,400 cubic meters a minute, up from 12,700, after the last gate set was commissioned in March. Authority chief Mara Ellison said the revised channel has cut spill losses by 14% and stabilized supply for 31 irrigation users across the lower plain.

The work cost $68 million, including $11 million for sediment removal and sensor automation. Contractors expect the final snag list to close by late August.

For the sector, the Morrow diversion is another sign that inland water operators are moving from ad hoc repairs to capital-heavy, telemetry-led asset management.
